title: Jude and the Veil
premise: When the wards sealing Thornbury Valley collapse, exiled storm-caller Dominic Thornbury discovers the valley was never a prison but a shield: his family's magic was traded away generations ago to the court beneath the mountain, and the price is now due. The stars went out because the Veil between worlds is being unpicked thread by thread, and among the souls already sold is Jude, a nameless foundling Dominic grew up with and secretly loved. To steal Jude's soul back, Dominic must bargain with the mountain court, break an inheritance contract written in his own blood, and choose between restoring his stolen birthright and tearing down a justice system that has never answered to anyone above ground. In the end he renounces the inheritance entirely, unmaking the contract and letting the storm return to everyone at once — which costs him his own name in the court's ledger, but frees Jude and relights the stars.
about_author: Tamsin Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing disputed land deeds before turning to fiction about contracts no one should have signed. She writes from a farmhouse on a fault line, which she insists is a coincidence.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On the eve of the valley's Founding Festival, every star vanishes at once, and the border wards — silent for thirty years — shatter like glass. Dominic, who has never crossed the valley line, feels his dormant storm-magic wake painfully in his bones. Emotional beat: dread mixed with a terrible exhilaration he's ashamed of.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were Hiding
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Investigating the fallen ward-stones, Dominic finds carvings older than the valley itself: a contract sigil bearing the Thornbury name. The village elders refuse to explain and order everyone indoors. Beat: the first crack in everything he believed about his exile — it was protection, or a cage, depending on who you ask.

chapters.title: Jude
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, in flashback woven through the present. Jude, the foundling raised in the valley with no recorded parentage, has always felt like a placeholder in someone else's story. Now Jude hears a voice through the broken wards calling a name that isn't 'Jude' at all. Beat: longing for an identity that might be a trap.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. His dying grandmother confesses: each generation of Thornburys sold something to the court beneath the mountain — land, luck, years, and finally people. Jude's soul was sold at birth to settle a debt Dominic's father incurred. Beat: grief curdling into fury at an inheritance built on other people's lives.

chapters.title: Crossing the Line
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Defying the elders, Dominic steps over the valley boundary for the first time, carrying a knife, his grandmother's contract-sigil, and Jude, who insists on coming. Outside, the world is starless, gray, and full of refugees fleeing something worse. Beat: vertigo of freedom without safety.

chapters.title: The Road of Unpaid Tolls
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the road, they learn whole villages have been 'collected' by the mountain court as payment for debts nobody remembers agreeing to. A hedge-witch named Marisol tells them the stars are being fed to the Veil to keep it open. Beat: the dawning scale of the injustice — their valley is one small account in a vast ledger.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They reach the mountain gate, where the court's steward, Lady Vess, greets Dominic by a name he's never heard: 'Thornbury-heir.' Inside, the court is beautiful, cold, and lit by caged starlight. Beat: seduction and horror — this place could give him everything except a clean conscience.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Vess offers a bargain: accept the full Thornbury inheritance — power, lands, restored magic — and Jude's debt is merely transferred, not erased. Refuse, and the court collects Jude at the next new moon. Beat: the trap of complicity dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Soul-Vaults
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. While Dominic negotiates, Jude is shown courtesy — and the vaults where sold souls are kept as pale flames in glass. Jude finds their own flame and realizes it burns the wrong color: someone tampered with it long ago. Beat: identity as evidence; hope sharpened by suspicion.

chapters.title: A Debt Older Than the Valley
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Digging in the court's archive, Dominic discovers the original contract wasn't signed by his ancestors willingly — the first Thornbury was coerced during a famine, and every renewal since has been forged. The court knows. The court has always known. Beat: righteous anger finding its legal footing.

chapters.title: Marisol's Price
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The hedge-witch reappears inside the mountain — she's been hunting the court for decades, since her sister's soul was taken. She offers Dominic the one loophole: a contract can be voided if the heir renounces the inheritance publicly and the wronged party testifies. But testimony requires a soul willing to speak, and speaking may destroy it. Beat: alliance forged in shared grief.

chapters.title: The Steward's Confession
chapters.summary: Lady Vess's POV. Vess, herself bound by a centuries-old contract, reveals she keeps the vaults not from cruelty but because she once tried to defy the court and lost everything. She warns Dominic: the court's true master is the Veil itself, and it is starving. Beat: the enemy revealed as another prisoner.

chapters.title: New Moon Notice
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The new moon arrives early — the court accelerates collection, claiming Dominic's snooping breached hospitality. Jude is summoned to the collection rite in three days. Beat: panic, and the collapse of any plan that relied on time.

chapters.title: What Jude Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Under pressure, Jude's sealed memories surface: they weren't sold at birth — they volunteered as an infant's proxy, a bargain made by a mother trying to save the rest of her children. Jude's real name surfaces with them. Beat: identity reclaimed, at the cost of learning love was always entangled with sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Renunciation
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Before the assembled court, Dominic publicly renounces the Thornbury inheritance, every acre and every advantage, invoking the old law Marisol unearthed. The court laughs — until the contract-sigil on his skin begins to burn away. Beat: triumph that immediately turns to terror as the court invokes its counter-clause.

chapters.title: Counter-Claim
chapters.summary: Lady Vess's POV. The court rules that a renunciation without testimony is void, and moves to collect both Jude and Dominic. Vess, choosing at last to betray her masters, unlocks the soul-vaults and tells Dominic the truth: the Veil doesn't want worship. It wants witnesses. Beat: betrayal inverted into rescue; stakes go cosmic.

chapters.title: Riot of Small Flames
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The freed souls, given momentary voice, testify in a roaring chorus — thousands of coerced contracts read aloud until the mountain shakes. The court's magistrates try to snuff the flames. Marisol holds the door. Beat: chaos as catharsis; justice erupting outside any lawful procedure.

chapters.title: Before the Veil
chapters.summary: Dominic and Jude's shared POV. At the mountain's heart, they face the Veil — a hungry seam between worlds wearing the face of the first Thornbury's creditor. It offers Dominic his inheritance back if he'll serve as its new steward. Beat: the final temptation, and the quiet certainty of refusal.

chapters.title: The Storm Returns to Everyone
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Instead of accepting power, Dominic does what his family never dared: he gives the storm-magic back — not to the court, not to the Veil, but to the sky, releasing it to all people equally. The contract, having nothing left to bind, unravels. Beat: self-annihilation as liberation; the climax's cost becomes clear.

chapters.title: The Cost of a Name
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The unraveling works — but the ledger demands balance, and it takes Dominic's name in exchange, erasing him from memory and record. Jude, holding the last trace of him, speaks his name aloud into the Veil and refuses to let it be collected. Beat: heartbreak defying erasure; love as testimony.

chapters.title: Stars, Relit
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The stars return one by one over the valley, the mountain, the refugee roads. The court beneath the mountain stands empty, its vaults open, its ledgers public. Survivors begin the slow work of restitution — returning what can be returned, mourning what cannot. Beat: exhausted, hard-won peace.

chapters.title: Jude and the Veil
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, epilogue. A year later, Jude tends the valley's new archive of freed contracts, teaching others to read the fine print of their lives. A stranger arrives with storm-grey eyes and no name he can recall — but when Jude says 'Dominic,' he smiles like the word fits. Beat: identity rebuilt not by blood or law, but by being witnessed and chosen.
